idiom_name: cdylib + entry fn returning a repr(C) vtable
implementation_notes: The portable baseline: the plugin crate is built as a cdylib and exports one #[no_mangle] extern "C" entry function returning a pointer to a #[repr(C)] struct of function pointers (or to a boxed object behind an opaque pointer), since Rust has no stable ABI and no runtime reflection. The host calls libloading::Library::new and Symbol::get to resolve the entry point, keeps the Library handle alive for as long as any code from it is reachable, and wraps every exported function with catch_unwind because unwinding across the C boundary is undefined behaviour. It is the only variant that lets plugins be written in other languages, at the price of hand-written marshalling and lifetime discipline.
pitfalls: Dropping the Library while a symbol or a value it created is still used segfaults; bundle the handle with the plugin object and order fields so the library is dropped last.
A panic that crosses the extern "C" boundary is undefined behaviour (abort at best), so every exported function needs catch_unwind or a panic-handling wrapper.
Rust types such as String, Vec and trait objects are not FFI-safe and their layout is unstable across compiler versions; only #[repr(C)] types and C-compatible pointers may cross.

variants.name: abi_stable RootModule with load-time layout checking
variants.implementation_notes: The Rust-to-Rust answer: the interface crate derives StableAbi on every type that crosses the boundary, the plugin implements RootModule (with declare_root_module_statics! and a shared BASE_NAME) and is loaded with RootModule::load_from_file, and the runtime checks the recorded layout of each type at load time so a plugin built against a different compiler or crate version is rejected instead of corrupting memory. abi_stable wraps libloading and adds sabi_trait for trait objects across the boundary, but its documented scope is plugin systems without support for unloading - it deliberately leaks the library on load to avoid use-after-free - so prefer it when correctness matters more than hot reload.
pitfalls: Every type crossing the boundary must derive StableAbi and use abi_stable's FFI-safe standard library types; a plain Vec or String inside a prefix struct is a compile error, and getting the wrapper types right is the real cost.

The library is intentionally leaked to avoid use-after-free, so plugin reload means restarting the process; likewise the abi_stable ABI itself is versioned per release and mismatches are caught only at load time.
